title: Final Settlement and Liquidation of Construction Contracts 2026
desc: Settlement and liquidation of construction contracts in 2026 under Decree 210/2026/ND-CP: A-B dossier, 60–120 and 45–90 day deadlines, unilateral settlement.
summary: How to settle and liquidate a construction contract after the work is finished under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 210/2026/ND-CP: dossier, deadlines, and what happens when one party does not cooperate.
body: Finishing the building does not mean the contract is finished: the two parties must still carry out final settlement (fixing the total amount payable) and liquidation (ending all rights and obligations). This article summarizes Article 87 of the Construction Law 2025 and Articles 30 and 31 of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP.
1. The contract must specify settlement and liquidation

A construction contract must specify payment, interim payment, final settlement, and liquidation, including cases of unilateral settlement and liquidation (Clause 1, Article 87). The contractor is responsible for final settlement with the employer within the period the parties agree (Clause 3).

The dossier is prepared by the contractor and confirmed by both parties (Clause 1, Article 30). The main components (mandatory for public investment and PPP projects; private houses should use them as a reference) are (Clause 2, Article 30):
Minutes of acceptance of completion of all work under the contract and of additional work;
The settlement value schedule (A–B settlement): the value of work completed under the contract, additional work, amounts already paid, interim payments, and the balance still payable;
As-built completion records (hoàn công) and the construction log (for contracts that include construction works);

For public investment and PPP projects: at most 60 days from the date all work is completed and accepted; for large or complex contracts this may be extended, but to no more than 120 days (Clause 3, Article 30). For private houses, the parties agree the deadline themselves.
A contract is liquidated when (Clause 2, Article 31):
The parties have completed their obligations under the contract; or

The contract is terminated under Clause 2, Article 85 of the Construction Law (force majeure where the contract cannot be amended; work suspended beyond the contract period through no fault of the other party, etc.).

The procedure, deadline, and form of liquidation are agreed by the parties (Clause 4, Article 87). For public investment and PPP projects: the parties may agree that the contract expires automatically once obligations are completed, or prepare liquidation minutes (prepared by the contractor and submitted to the employer for confirmation); the liquidation deadline is at most 45 days, or at most 90 days for large or complex contracts (Clause 3, Article 31).
5. When one party refuses to settle or liquidate

If one party does not carry out settlement or liquidation as agreed, the other party has the right to settle and liquidate unilaterally (Clause 5, Article 87). In that case, the unilateral party prepares the settlement dossier and carries out liquidation in accordance with the contract (Clause 1, Article 30; Clause 1, Article 31). The contract should therefore state clearly: after how many days without a response the other party may settle unilaterally.
Keep all stage acceptance minutes, payment records, and written approvals of additional work for cross-checking at settlement.

Ask the contractor to hand over the as-built completion dossier, which is needed to register the house on the land use right certificate (sổ đỏ) (see As-built completion and registering a house on the land use right certificate).
Any retention money for warranty (if held back) is paid only after the agreed warranty period ends.

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. The dossier components and the 60–120 day (settlement) and 45–90 day (liquidation) deadlines are mandatory only for contracts of public investment and PPP projects. For contracts signed and being performed before 1 July 2026 (projects not using public investment capital), the parties may agree to apply Decree 210/2026/ND-CP; if they cannot agree, the rules in force at signing apply (Clause 2, Article 33).
